parsed.explanation: The quote appears verbatim in the write-up's "Current best" section, and in context it is the author explicitly flagging the finiteness claim as an open need ("Need a rigorous proof that (1) only finitely many primes can ever be forced as new restrictions"). Scanning the whole text: the only support for finiteness is computational ("Pattern: finitely many 'essential' primes seem to determine an eventual modulus L") and explicitly labelled "Conjecture", with the "Full proof" section stating "(Not yet complete.)". No large-prime-erasure argument — showing any term divisible by a large prime is dominated by a smaller admissible number with the same small-prime support — is written anywhere, for any case. Hence obligation (F) is unwritten, and without it no finite L exists, so periodicity is unestablished.
